patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with lifelong atopy (eczema, allergic rhinitis) and recurrent HSV-1 cold sores, who had intraoperative anaphylaxis as a child and again at a 2025 nevus excision, later traced to latex. HSV keratitis of the right eye in October 2025 healed without sequelae.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, ESTABLISHING CARE

32-year-old woman, elementary school teacher, transferring from her previous primary office. No acute complaints today. Wants one place to call when her allergies or skin act up.

HISTORY
Eczema since she was a toddler. These days it is mostly hands and the creases of the elbows in winter, and the mometasone ointment keeps it quiet; she uses it a few days at a time, not continuously. Moisturizes with a fragrance-free cream.
Allergies: itchy watery eyes and congestion every spring with the trees, plus a year-round stuffy nose she was told was dust mite. Daily fluticasone, cetirizine on bad days.
Cold sores since her teens, roughly two or three a year. Keeps valacyclovir at home and starts it at the first tingle.
At 8 she had her tonsils and adenoids out and had a severe allergic reaction in the OR. Her mother was told it was anaphylaxis but no one ever told them what caused it. She has never had testing. No reactions to any medicine since that she knows of.

PSH: T&A age 8 (reaction as above).
Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment BID PRN; cetirizine 10 mg daily PRN; fluticasone nasal 1 spray each side daily; valacyclovir 1 g at prodrome then 1 g 12 h later.
Allergies: dust mite and tree pollen (rhinitis). No known drug allergies.
Family: mother asthma and hay fever; father eczema; younger sister also gets cold sores.
Social: teaches elementary school. Never smoked. A glass of wine once or twice a month. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. No wheeze or asthma symptoms of her own.

EXAM
Well appearing. HEENT: TMs clear, mild pale nasal turbinates, oropharynx clear, lips without lesions. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: a few faint dry patches at both antecubital fossae, no excoriation or weeping. No edema.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Atopic dermatitis, quiet right now. Continue mometasone in short bursts, daily emollient.
2. Allergic rhinitis, perennial with spring flares. Continue fluticasone daily and cetirizine as needed.
3. Recurrent herpes labialis. Episodic valacyclovir, refills on file.
4. History of anaphylaxis during childhood surgery, cause unknown. Advised she tell any surgeon or dentist about it before a procedure.
5. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids; one-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, which she agrees to. Requesting records from her prior office, including her last Pap and immunizations. PHQ-2 negative.
Lab draw Monday morning. Follow up for a physical next year or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your Recent Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, everything from Monday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were both negative. Nothing to change. Nice meeting you last week.

- Problem list: eczema, allergic rhinitis, recurrent cold sores, remote anaphylaxis during childhood surgery.

No childhood surgical records in the packet. Placed in chart for PCP review.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Hands cracking and itchy since the holidays, worse with all the handwashing in the classroom and the dry heat at school. Elbow creases flaring too. Using the mometasone most nights for about a week, which helps, but it comes back when she stops. No oozing, no crusting, no fever. Sleep a little broken by the itch.
O: Vitals as charted. Dorsal hands with dry, lichenified erythematous plaques and a few fissures over the knuckles; both antecubital fossae with mild erythema and scale. No vesicles, no honey crust, no pustules.
A: Atopic dermatitis, winter flare, hands and flexures. No sign of infection.
P: Mometasone twice daily for two weeks, then weekends only for a few weeks. Heavy plain ointment after every wash and cotton gloves over it at night. Keep a fragrance-free hand cream at her desk. If the hands are not better in three weeks, message me and we can talk about dermatology.

documents.title: Allergy Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the trees are out and I am a mess. Could you send refills of the nasal spray and the cetirizine? My hands are fine now, the gloves trick worked. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Allergy Refills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done, both sent with a year of refills. During the worst of the pollen it is fine to take the cetirizine every day rather than as needed. Glad the hands settled.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: good year. One mild cold sore in the spring that she caught early with valacyclovir. Hands stayed decent since the winter flare. Allergies typical for the spring, controlled on the spray. No ER visits, no new meds.

Current meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN, cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, valacyclovir episodic.
Allergies: dust mite, tree pollen. NKDA.
Social: back in the classroom. Never smoker, rare alcohol. Walking most evenings.

ROS negative in detail. Periods regular.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Pleasant, well. HEENT normal, lips clear. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen benign. Skin with faint dryness of the knuckles only. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.

A/P:
- Adult preventive care: PHQ-2 0. Pap/HPV co-test was negative in 2021; next one due 2026. Tdap 2019, current. Flu and updated COVID given today.
- Atopic dermatitis, controlled. Same plan; start the night-glove routine early this winter.
- Allergic rhinitis, stable.
- Recurrent cold sores, infrequent. Valacyclovir refilled.
- Remote anaphylaxis, cause unknown. Reminded her to flag it before any procedure.
- CBC, CMP and lipids drawn today. Physical again in a year.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, labs from Thursday's physical were all normal, cholesterol included. See you next year, or anytime you need us.

documents.title: RE: Cold Sore Starting

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two weeks of sneezing, itchy eyes and a blocked nose, the usual tree season but heavier this year. Using fluticasone most days, not every day. Cetirizine helps the itch. No fever, no facial pain, no cough or wheeze, no discolored drainage.
O: Vitals as charted. Conjunctivae mildly injected, no discharge. Nasal mucosa pale and boggy, clear rhinorrhea. Sinuses nontender. Pharynx clear. Lungs clear, no wheeze.
A: Allergic rhinitis, seasonal flare on a perennial background.
P: Fluticasone every day through June, aimed toward the outer wall of each nostril. Cetirizine daily for now. Saline rinse after outdoor recess duty. Return if facial pain or fever.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Last week of summer before teachers report. Feels well. Two cold sores this year, both handled at home. Hands held up last winter. Spring allergies settled after the April visit.

New concern: a mole on her upper back that her sister noticed at the beach. She cannot see it herself and does not know if it has been there long. Would like a skin doctor to look at it and do a full skin check.

Meds: mometasone ointment PRN, cetirizine PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, valacyclovir episodic.
Allergies: dust mite, tree pollen. NKDA.
Social: unchanged. Never smoker.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT clear, lips without lesions. Neck supple. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Skin: on the left upper back a single brown papule, about 6 mm, round, even color; no other notable lesions on the trunk or limbs. Faint dryness of the elbow creases.

A/P:
- Preventive: PHQ-2 0. CMP and lipids today. Pap due 2026. Flu and COVID at a nurse visit when this year's vaccines arrive.
- Nevus, left upper back: referred to dermatology for evaluation and a full skin exam, at her request.
- Atopic dermatitis and allergic rhinitis: stable on current regimen.
- Herpes labialis: episodic valacyclovir.
- History of childhood anaphylaxis during surgery: if dermatology plans to remove anything, she should tell them about it ahead of time.
Physical again next summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted this morning; seen same day. Three days of sore blisters on her lips and a few inside her cheek. Similar to past episodes. Eating is uncomfortable. She did not feel the usual warning tingle, so she never took her valacyclovir. Over the years she has had these two or three times a year, though this past year fewer. No fever, no eye symptoms, no genital lesions. She denies any recent sexual activity or new partner. Her dermatology appointment for the back mole is coming up; she wants to make sure this clears first.
O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Clusters of small vesicles on a red base along the vermilion of the upper and lower lip, and a few of the same on the right buccal mucosa. No gingival involvement. No cervical or submandibular nodes. Eyes clear. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.
A: Herpes simplex, orolabial with buccal lesions, in a patient with a long history of cold sores. Checking type-specific serology to confirm the type, and a CBC.
P: Valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 7 days. Mouth care: salt-water rinses, soft cool foods. Stay home from school until lesions crust if she can. CBC and HSV-1/HSV-2 IgG today. Call if eye pain, redness or blurred vision, or if not improving in a week.

documents.title: HSV Blood Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, blood count is normal. Your antibody test shows HSV type 1, the usual cold-sore virus, and no type 2. That fits with your history and with what we saw on Monday. Keep going with the full week of valacyclovir. How is your mouth feeling?

documents.title: RE: HSV Blood Test Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Much better, the inside ones are almost gone and the lip is crusting. Thank you for squeezing me in.

documents.title: Mole on My Back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update: saw the dermatologist last week. They want to cut the mole out to be safe and scheduled it for January 16, after break and once the cold sore stuff is well behind me. I told them about my reaction as a kid. Do you need anything from me before then?

documents.title: RE: Mole on My Back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Nothing needed from us. I have not received their note yet; I'll keep an eye out. Good that you told them about the childhood reaction.

documents.title: Bad Reaction Yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted you to know: when they were finishing taking the mole off my back yesterday, I suddenly felt my throat closing, my face swelled up and I broke out in hives everywhere. They gave me a shot and IV fluids and sent me by ambulance to the ER. They watched me for hours and let me go home last night with an EpiPen. I feel washed out but OK. I am taking today off. It felt like what my mom described from when I was 8, but worse.

documents.title: RE: Bad Reaction Yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I am so sorry, that sounds frightening. Glad you are home. Any return of throat tightness, trouble breathing or swelling: use the auto-injector and call 911. I'd like to see you next week; the front desk will call with a time. I'll request the records from the procedure and the ER.

conditions.label: Anaphylaxis
conditions.note: during excision of back nevus at an outside procedure suite; trigger not yet identified

medications.sig: Inject 0.3 mg into the outer thigh once for anaphylaxis; may repeat once after 5 to 15 minutes; call 911

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up one week after a reaction during excision of the nevus on her left upper back at an outside dermatology procedure suite on 1/16. By her account, near the end of the procedure she felt her throat tighten, her face and eyes swelled, she broke out in itchy hives everywhere and could not get a full breath. The team gave an injection in her thigh and started an IV, and she went by ambulance to the ER, was watched for several hours and sent home with an epinephrine auto-injector. She was told the reaction was anaphylaxis. Nobody has told her what caused it. Back at work since Monday. No symptoms since. The excision site is healing; sutures out next week at dermatology.
This is her second reaction during a procedure; the first was at age 8. She remembers no common thread except being in an operating room.
We have not yet received the procedure or ER records; requested again today. Pharmacy confirms an epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector two-pack filled 1/16 from the ER prescriber.
O: Vitals as charted. Comfortable. No facial or lip swelling, no urticaria. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Left upper back: healing linear incision with sutures, no erythema or drainage. Lips without lesions.
A: 1. Anaphylaxis during a skin procedure, resolved. Two perioperative episodes now; a procedure-related trigger needs to be found before she has anything else done.
2. Herpes labialis from October healed.
P: Referral to allergy and immunology. Reviewed auto-injector use with her trainer pen; carry two at all times, school nurse to be told. No elective procedures or dental work beyond cleanings until the allergy evaluation is done. Will follow the pathology from dermatology.

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Event Record
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL ALLERGY AND IMMUNOLOGY SERVICE, PROCEDURE AREA RECORD
Date of event: 01/16/2025
Patient: Lisa O'Brien, 34 F

Called emergently to the outpatient procedure suite. Patient under local anesthesia for excisional biopsy of a nevus on the left upper back, wound being closed, when she abruptly reported her throat was closing, then developed facial swelling, trouble breathing and a generalized itchy rash. Reports a similar but milder reaction during surgery in childhood.
Allergies on file: dust mite (rhinitis), tree pollen (rhinitis).
Home meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN, cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, valacyclovir episodic for cold sores (recently completed a course for herpes labialis).
Family: atopy in both parents.
Vitals on arrival: BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: bilateral periorbital edema, diffuse urticaria over trunk and limbs, expiratory wheeze both lungs. No JVD. No peripheral edema.
Treatment: epinephrine 0.5 mg IM, lateral thigh. Peripheral IV placed; normal saline bolus started. Transferred to the emergency department for observation.
Impression: anaphylaxis, intraoperative, during minor skin procedure. Agent unclear; exposures during the case included local anesthetic, skin prep, gloves and dressings.
Recommendations: observe in ED; discharge with epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg; outpatient allergy evaluation; until then, flag chart for anaphylaxis during procedures.
No emergency department note was included in this packet.

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Consultation
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ALLERGY AND IMMUNOLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 03/04/2025
Re: Lisa O'Brien, DOB 03/15/1990

Thank you for referring Ms. O'Brien, a 34-year-old teacher with atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis and recurrent HSV-1 labialis, after anaphylaxis on 1/16/2025 during excision of a back nevus. She also reacted during a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy at age 8. Between those, she has had dental cleanings and routine care without trouble.

Current allergies: dust mite and tree pollen (rhinitis).
Meds: mometasone ointment PRN, cetirizine PRN (held 5 days before visit), fluticasone nasal, valacyclovir episodic, epinephrine auto-injector.
Exam today: normal, no urticaria, lungs clear.

Testing: latex-specific IgE 5.2 kU/L, positive.

Impression: IgE-mediated latex allergy with anaphylaxis. Both intraoperative reactions are best explained by latex exposure (gloves, drains, catheters). Local anesthetic allergy is unlikely and was not pursued.

Recommendations:
1. Strict latex avoidance. Every surgical, dental and procedural visit must be latex-free; she has a letter to give to all providers.
2. Carry two epinephrine auto-injectors at all times, including at school.
3. Medical alert bracelet recommended.
4. Follow up here as needed.

Allergies updated in our records: LATEX (anaphylaxis), dust mite, tree pollen.

reports.text: Specimen: skin, left upper back, excision. Gross: ellipse of skin 1.4 x 0.6 cm, with a centrally placed 0.6 cm brown papule. Microscopic: nests of banal melanocytes at the dermoepidermal junction and within the dermis, maturing with depth. No cytologic atypia, no mitoses, no pagetoid spread. Margins free of the lesion.
reports.conclusion: Benign compound melanocytic nevus, margins clear.

documents.title: Dermatopathology Report Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pathology report for the 01/16/2025 left upper back excision received by fax after a second request to the dermatology office. Report dated 01/21/2025. Scanned for PCP review.

documents.title: Pathology Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Benign compound nevus, completely removed. Messaged patient.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Tree pollen season again: sneezing, itchy eyes, congestion for ten days. Using fluticasone daily and cetirizine daily this time, about 70% better. Saw allergy in early March; their letter came last month. Latex allergy confirmed and both OR reactions blamed on it. She has her latex-free letter, wears a medical alert bracelet now and keeps two auto-injectors in her school bag. She is relieved to have an answer. Pathology from the back was benign.
O: Vitals as charted. Pale boggy turbinates, clear drainage. Mild conjunctival injection. Lungs clear. Back scar well healed.
A: 1. Allergic rhinitis, seasonal flare, partly controlled.
2. Latex allergy with anaphylaxis, now identified; added to the allergy list today. January's anaphylaxis episode closed; history of anaphylaxis stays on the problem list.
P: Add saline rinses; continue daily fluticasone and cetirizine through the season. Chart flagged latex-free for any procedure here, including immunizations and blood draws. Auto-injector renewals through us going forward.

documents.title: Form for School
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Our school nurse needs a form signed by my doctor so I can keep my auto-injectors in the classroom and so she has an emergency plan on file for me. I attached the blank one. Thank you!

documents.title: Medication Authorization for School
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the school nurse:
Lisa O'Brien (DOB 03/15/1990) has a latex allergy with a history of anaphylaxis. She is authorized to carry and self-administer epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injectors at work. In an emergency: inject into the outer thigh, call 911, and a second dose may be given after 5 to 15 minutes if symptoms persist. Please keep latex balloons and latex gloves out of her classroom and the nurse's office supplies she may use.
Form completed and signed; returned to patient through the portal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: big year. Anaphylaxis in January during the nevus excision; allergy found latex IgE positive in March. Nevus benign. No reactions since. Carries two auto-injectors, school has her plan. One small cold sore over the summer, treated at home. Eczema quiet through the warm months. Allergies better this spring with daily spray.

Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; valacyclovir 1 g episodic; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen (rhinitis).
Social: started the new school year last month. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

ROS: negative.
Exam: Vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal; lips clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. Skin: well-healed linear scar left upper back; no eczema active today. No edema.

A/P:
- Preventive: PHQ-9 1. CBC, CMP, lipids today. Flu and COVID given, latex-free supplies confirmed before the injections. Pap/HPV co-test due next year.
- Latex allergy with history of anaphylaxis: avoidance, auto-injectors current; renewal due in January.
- Atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, herpes labialis: stable, no changes.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, all of last week's bloodwork is normal. Have a good fall.

documents.title: Eye Problem
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I ended up in the ER yesterday with my right eye. It had been red and painful for three days and getting blurry, and the light was killing me. The eye doctor there said it was herpes on the cornea, the same virus as my cold sores, and gave me an antiviral eye gel to use 5 times a day. I have a follow-up with them next week. I am out of school for a few days. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Eye Problem
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry, that is a painful one. Use the gel exactly as they told you and keep the follow-up with ophthalmology; they will guide how long to continue it. Don't touch the eye and then your lips or the other eye, and wash hands after the gel. If vision gets worse or the pain spikes before your appointment, go back to them. Please book a visit with me after you've seen them.

medications.sig: 1 drop in the right eye 5 times daily until the ulcer heals, then 3 times daily for 7 days

documents.title: Emergency Department Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, OPHTHALMOLOGY CONSULT
Date of service: 10/14/2025
Patient: Lisa O'Brien, 35 F

CC: right eye pain, redness, blurred vision x 3 days.
HPI: 35-year-old woman with recurrent HSV-1 cold sores (orolabial outbreak with buccal lesions October 2024) and anaphylaxis during a skin procedure in January 2025, attributed to latex. Three days ago it felt like something was in the right eye; then tearing, light sensitivity, worsening pain and blur. No trauma. No contact lens use. Left eye fine.
PMH: atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, recurrent herpes labialis, anaphylaxis history.
Meds: mometasone ointment PRN, cetirizine PRN, fluticasone nasal, valacyclovir episodic, epinephrine auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen.

Exam:
Visual acuity (sc): OD 20/60, OS 20/20.
Pupils equal and reactive, no APD.
OD: conjunctival injection. Cornea with several small epithelial vesicles and a branching dendritic ulcer that takes up fluorescein. No purulent discharge. Anterior chamber deep and quiet.
OS: normal anterior segment.
IOP normal both eyes.

Impression: herpes simplex epithelial keratitis, right eye.
Plan: ganciclovir 0.15% ophthalmic gel, 1 drop OD 5 times daily until the epithelium heals, then 3 times daily for 7 days. No topical steroid. Ophthalmology clinic follow-up in about 10 days. Return sooner for worsening vision or pain.
Latex precautions observed during the exam.

events.reason: follow-up after ED visit for eye

conditions.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
conditions.note: right eye, dendritic epithelial ulcer, treated by ophthalmology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here after her 10/14 ER visit for the right eye. ER ophthalmology note received 10/30: dendritic ulcer right cornea, acuity 20/60 on that side, started on ganciclovir gel. She saw ophthalmology clinic on 10/24 and was told the ulcer had healed and her vision was back; she finished the 3-times-a-day taper last week. We do not yet have the clinic note. The eye feels normal now, no pain, no redness, reading fine. No new lip lesions.
O: Vitals as charted. Right eye white and quiet, no discharge, pupils equal. Reads the wall chart comfortably at near. Lips clear.
A: Herpes simplex keratitis, right eye, treated and healed per ophthalmology. Recurrent HSV-1 labialis.
P: Added to the problem list. Requested the ophthalmology clinic note. Any recurrence of eye pain, redness or blur goes straight to ophthalmology, not to waiting on us. Continue episodic valacyclovir for lip outbreaks. She will keep her ophthalmology follow-up schedule.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY CLINIC
Date of visit: 10/24/2025
Re: Lisa O'Brien, DOB 03/15/1990

Seen in follow-up for right herpes simplex epithelial keratitis diagnosed in the emergency department 10/14/2025, on ganciclovir 0.15% gel 5 times daily.
Today: pain and photophobia resolved.
Visual acuity: OD 20/20, OS 20/20.
Slit lamp OD: corneal epithelium healed, no residual staining with fluorescein; no stromal haze or infiltrate; anterior chamber quiet.
OS: normal.
Assessment: HSV epithelial keratitis OD, resolved.
Plan: reduce ganciclovir to 3 times daily for 7 days, then stop. Return promptly for any recurrence of redness, pain or blurred vision in either eye.
Allergies: latex (anaphylaxis); dust mite; tree pollen.

(Received by fax 01/08/2026 after a second request.)

documents.title: Prior Authorization and Renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting a new prescription for epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injectors; her two-pack from January 2025 expires this month. Insurance prefers the generic; brand would need a PA. PCP sent generic, 2 two-packs (one for home, one for school), 1 refill. Patient notified by portal; she will drop the old pens off at the pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Eczema up for three weeks with the cold snap: backs of the hands, wrists and elbow creases, itchy at night. Using mometasone on and off, plus hand cream, but she slipped on the night gloves. Has been extra careful about not using latex gloves for classroom cleanup. Eye has stayed fine since the fall. No cold sores this winter.
O: Vitals as charted. Dorsal hands and wrists with erythematous, scaly, slightly lichenified patches; a couple of shallow fissures. Antecubital fossae with mild erythema. No vesicles, crusts or pustules. Eyes white and quiet.
A: Atopic dermatitis, winter flare. Herpes simplex keratitis resolved; ophthalmology clinic letter arrived in January confirming healed cornea and 20/20.
P: Mometasone twice daily for 2 weeks, then twice weekly maintenance on the usual spots through March. Back to the ointment-and-cotton-glove routine at night. Vinyl or nitrile gloves only. Message in 3 weeks if not clearly better. Physical this summer with Pap.

documents.title: Spring Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen season is here again. Could I get refills on the fluticasone and cetirizine? Hands cleared up nicely after the February visit.

documents.title: RE: Spring Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Both sent to your pharmacy per the doctor, with refills for the year. Your physical is booked for July 30 at 7:30 AM.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: quiet year after a rough 2025. No allergic reactions; auto-injectors renewed in January and never needed. No eye trouble since the keratitis healed in October. Two small cold sores, both caught early with valacyclovir. Eczema flare in February settled. Spring allergies manageable with daily spray and cetirizine.

Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; valacyclovir 1 g episodic; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen (rhinitis).
Social: summer off, teaching again in late August. Never smoker; alcohol rare.

ROS negative.
Exam: Vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, eyes white, lips clear. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected with a nonlatex speculum and gloves. Skin: hands clear, old scar left upper back. No edema.

A/P:
- Preventive: PHQ-2 0. Pap with HPV co-test today (last 2021). CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and COVID this fall; she will come by once vaccines arrive.
- Latex allergy with anaphylaxis history: avoidance, auto-injectors current.
- Atopic dermatitis: controlled; keep the winter routine.
- Allergic rhinitis: stable.
- Recurrent HSV-1 labialis: episodic valacyclovir, refills sent. History of HSV keratitis right eye, healed; she knows to go straight to ophthalmology for eye symptoms.
Follow-up in the fall for skin and allergies, then physical next summer.

documents.title: Physical Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, your Pap and HPV test are both normal, so the next one is in five years. Blood counts, chemistry and cholesterol from the 30th are all normal too. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

documents.title: RE: Physical Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news, thank you! See you in November.
